_comment: Erase-and-retype corpus. The documents are GENERATED by
tests/fixtures/make-fixtures.mjs, so this project owns them outright and
every rect below is the exact box the text was drawn at — a failing case
means the eraser missed, never that a coordinate was measured a pixel out.
tier1 = the words are in the page's text layer, so the background under
them can be recovered exactly by re-rendering without those glyphs. These
must come out clean; anything above a whisker of residue is a real bug.
tier2 = the words are pixels inside an image. Nothing can recover the
background, so the numbers here record where reconstruction actually
stands rather than asserting it is good.

fixtures.name: letter
fixtures.note: Generated A4 letter: coloured body text over white, a rule under a coloured run, a filled colour band, and a speckled raster strip with lettering baked into it.

targets.label: bold dark-blue run mid-sentence
targets.why: bold + coloured, with a '!' immediately after it that an over-wide erase eats
targets.editWhy: shorter, to uncover the patch behind a text-layer erase

targets.label: 'Saturday' bold heading
targets.why: short bold run, tests that a small target isn't over-erased

targets.label: green run with an underline rule
targets.why: coloured text WITH a rule beneath it — the rule is not text and must survive

targets.label: run inside a filled colour band
targets.why: the patch has to take the band's colour, not the paper's

targets.label: white title baked into the speckled strip
targets.why: words that are pixels: nothing can recover this background

targets.label: a line set in the document's OWN embedded face
targets.why: the path almost every real PDF takes: the page embeds a subset of a real font program, so the editor should harvest that face and re-set the words in it (usableFace) rather than reach for a metric twin from the palette. The whole corpus was base-14 before this, which pdf-lib does not embed, so nothing here ever reached that code
targets.editTo: Set in the document's own harvested face
targets.editWhy: longer than the original, so a width error shows as overrun instead of hiding inside the old box

targets.label: 34pt display type in the embedded face
targets.why: the same path at display size. A per-character error that is a whisker at 11pt is a whole letterform at 34 — which is how the benchmark CV's 50pt name failed, and why a corpus of 11pt body copy could not see it

targets.label: light type on a coloured panel between two dark lines
targets.why: the shape that made retype reprint words in the colour of the thing behind them. The ink sampler judges ink-vs-paper against the median of a frame around the run; where that frame reaches into darker neighbours the median comes out dark, the lighter tone wins, and the 'ink' returned is the PANEL. The run is erased and redrawn invisible, and the app calls it a match. The suite catches it through inkRatio: an invisible reprint lays down no ink at all
targets.editTo: Light type, reset on the same panel
targets.editWhy: an edit as well as an identity pass, because the colour is chosen on both paths
